title: Rama finds Seetha's flowers and jewelry
introduction: Rama finds Seetha's flowers and footprints, followed by heavy footprints of some male massive demon. On detailed probing there appear some more ruins of a combat between two warriors. Concluding that Seetha is definitely abducted by a massive demon, Rama wants to countermove the universe, even by waging a war with gods.
closing: इति वाल्मीकि रामायणे आदि काव्ये अरण्य काण्डे चतुः षष्टितमः सर्गः
Thus, this is the 64th chapter in Aranya Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the first Epic poem of India

verses.devanagari:
स दीनो दीनया वाचा लक्ष्मणम् वाक्यम् अब्रवीत् |
शीघ्रम् लक्ष्मण जानीहि गत्वा गोदावरीम् नदीम्
अपि गोदावरीम् सीता पद्मानि आनयितुम् गता |
verses.iast:
sa dīno dīnayā vācā lakṣmaṇam vākyam abravīt |
śīghram lakṣmaṇa jānīhi gatvā godāvarīm nadīm
api godāvarīm sītā padmāni ānayitum gatā |
verses.translation: A pitiable one, such as he is, he spoke to Lakshmana in a pitiable voice, "Lakshmana, go quickly to River Godavari and find out whether Seetha has gone to Godavari to fetch lotuses..."

glosses.meaning: quickly, to Godavari, river, on going to

verses.devanagari:
एवम् उक्तः तु रामेण लक्ष्मणः पुनः एव हि
नदीम् गोदावरीम् रम्याम् जगाम लघु विक्रमः |
verses.iast:
evam uktaḥ tu rāmeṇa lakṣmaṇaḥ punaḥ eva hi
nadīm godāvarīm ramyām jagāma laghu vikramaḥ |
verses.translation: When Rama said thus to him Lakshmana again went to the charming River Godavari quickening his pace.

glosses.meaning: by Rama, thus, one who is said
in briskness, becoming valiant one - quickening his pace

verses.devanagari:
ताम् लक्ष्मणः तीर्थवतीम् विचित्वा रामम् अब्रवीत्
नैनाम् पश्यामि तीर्थेषु क्रोशतो न शृणोति मे |
verses.iast:
tām lakṣmaṇaḥ tīrthavatīm vicitvā rāmam abravīt
nainām paśyāmi tīr.htheṣu krośato na śṛṇoti me |
verses.translation: Searching at many declivities which River Godavari has on its banks Lakshmana said to Rama, "I do not espy her at ghats, declivities of riverbanks, and she is not replying though I shouted for her.

glosses.meaning: she which has many declivities, ghats

verses.devanagari:
कम् नु सा देशम् आपन्ना वैदेही क्लेश नाशिनी
न हि तम् वेद्मि वै राम यत्र सा तनु मध्यमा |
verses.iast:
kam nu sā deśam āpannā vaidehī kleśa nāśinī
na hi tam vedmi vai rāma yatra sā tanu madhyamā |
verses.translation: "In fact, oh, Rama, to which place she that neutraliser of nervousness, namely Vaidehi, has got round to, or where that frailty is, that place is really incomprehensible to me...

glosses.meaning: that [place,] not, I am [not able to] know of - beyond my knowledge]

verses.devanagari:
लक्ष्मणस्य वचः श्रुत्वा दीनः संताप मोहितः
रामः समभिचक्राम स्वयम् गोदावरीम् नदीम् |
स ताम् उपस्थितो रामः क्व सीते इति एवम् अब्रवीत्
verses.iast:
lakṣmaṇasya vacaḥ śrutvā dīnaḥ saṃtāpa mohitaḥ
rāmaḥ samabhicakrāma svayam godāvarīm nadīm |
sa tām upasthito rāmaḥ kva sīte iti evam abravīt
verses.translation: Rama who is already stupefied by anguish is now despaired on listening Lakshmana's words and he personally went straight to River Godavari, and staying nearby that river Rama shouted in this way, "Seetha... where are you?"

verses.devanagari:
भूतानि राक्षसेन्द्रेण वध अर्हेण हृताम् अपि |
न ताम् शशंसू रामाय तथा गोदावरी नदी
verses.iast:
bhūtāni rākṣasendreṇa vadha arheṇa hṛtām api |
na tām śaśaṃsū rāmāya tathā godāvarī nadī
verses.translation: The forest creatures which were asked earlier have not said to Rama that a deservedly destructible demagogue of demons has divested him of Seetha, likewise now River Godavari which is now being asked has not informed Rama about Seetha.

glosses.meaning: to be eliminated, who deserves to be
even [now,] Godavari, river [which is being asked]

verses.devanagari:
ततः प्रचोदिता भूतैः शंस च अस्मै प्रियाम् इति |
न च सा हि अवदत् सीताम् पृष्टा रामेण शोचता
verses.iast:
tataḥ pracoditā bhūtaiḥ śaṃsa ca asmai priyām iti |
na ca sā hi avadat sītām pṛṣṭā rāmeṇa śocatā
verses.translation: Though the woeful Rama has asked her, and even though all the georgic beings impelled her to inform Rama the fact about his ladylove, River Godavari then remained mouthless about Seetha.

glosses.meaning: by woeful, Rama, she who is asked
about ladylove, to him, inform, also, thus [tell Rama the fact of Seetha's abduction]

verses.devanagari:
रावणस्य च तत् रूपम् कर्माणि च दुरात्मनः |
ध्यात्वा भयात् तु वैदेहीम् सा नदी न शशंस ह
verses.iast:
rāvaṇasya ca tat rūpam kar.hmāṇi ca durātmanaḥ |
dhyātvā bhayāt tu vaidehīm sā nadī na śaśaṃsa ha
verses.translation: She that River Godavari has not informed Rama about Vaidehi just out of fear on recalling the mien and manoeuvres of malefic-minded Ravana, lest Ravana may drain her away.

verses.devanagari:
निराशः तु तया नद्या सीताया दर्शने कृतः |
उवाच रामः सौमित्रिम् सीता दर्शन कर्शितः
verses.iast:
nirāśaḥ tu tayā nadyā sītāyā dar.hśane kṛtaḥ |
uvāca rāmaḥ saumitrim sītā darśana karśitaḥ
verses.translation: Rama who is already in a rundown condition owing to the non-appearance of Seetha, is further rendered as a hopeless being by River Godavari in the matter of his catching a glimpse of Seetha, and such a Rama spoke to Saumitri.

glosses.meaning: Seetha, in not, appearance, who is run-down
by her, by that river, on her part
regarding getting a glimpse of her

verses.devanagari:
एषा गोदावरी सौम्य किंचन् न प्रतिभाषते |
किम् नु लक्ष्मण वक्ष्यामि समेत्य जनकम् वचः
मातरम् चैव वैदेह्या विना ताम् अहम् अप्रियम् |
verses.iast:
eṣā godāvarī saumya kiñcan na pratibhāṣate |
kim nu lakṣmaṇa vakṣyāmi sametya janakam vacaḥ
mātaram caiva vaidehyā vinā tām aham apriyam |
verses.translation: "Oh, kind Lakshmana, this Godavari is talking to me anything but a reply. In the absence of Vaidehi, oh Lakshmana, really what is that unpleasant word I have to say to Vaidehi's father king Janaka, also thus to Vaidehi's mother-in-law and my mother Kausalya, when I meet them!

glosses.meaning: anything, not, in turn, talking - replying

verses.devanagari:
या मे राज्य विहीनस्य वने वन्येन जीवतः
सर्वम् व्यपनयत् शोकम् वैदेही क्व नु सा गता |
verses.iast:
yā me rājya vihīnasya vane vanyena jīvataḥ
sarvam vyapanayat śokam vaidehī kva nu sā gatā |
verses.translation: "Which Vaidehi is the remover of all my sadness who am a destitute of kingdom and surviving in forests on forest produce, such as she is, where has she gone, really!

glosses.meaning: kingdom, one who is destitute of
in forests, on forest produce, surviving
she, to where, went to, really.

verses.devanagari:
ज्ञाति वर्ग विहीनस्य राज पुत्रीम् अपश्यतः
मन्ये दीर्घा भविष्यन्ति रात्रयो मम जाग्रतः |
verses.iast:
GYāti varga vihīnasya rāja putrīm apaśyataḥ
manye dīrghā bhaviṣyanti rātrayo mama jāgrataḥ |
verses.translation: "Though I am distanced from my relatives I deemed that princess Seetha alone would be an evermore relative of mine. But now when that princess alone is unseen I deem that my sleepless nights would be lengthy.

glosses.meaning: lengthy, they will become, I think.

verses.devanagari:
मंदाकिनीम् जनस्थानम् इमम् प्रस्रवणम् गिरिम्
सर्वाणि अनुचरिष्यामि यदि सीता हि लभ्यते |
verses.iast:
maṃdākinīm janasthānam imam prasravaṇam girim
sar.hvāṇi anucariṣyāmi yadi sītā hi labhyate |
verses.translation: "I will search all these places of Godavari, Janasthaana and this mountain with many rapids, perhaps Seetha may be available somewhere.
notes: River Mandakini is River Ganga and here River Godavari is said as Ganga as there are five Ganga-s panca gangaa Cauvery, Tungabhadra, Krishna Veni, Gautami [namely Godavari,] Bhaagiirathi. in Southern India and these are held sacred on par with River Ganga.

glosses.meaning: in tow [of Seetha,] I wish to ramble - I will search

verses.devanagari:
एते महा मृगा वीर माम् ईक्षन्ते पुनः पुनः
वक्तु कामा इह हि मे इंगितानि अनुपलक्षये |
verses.iast:
ete mahā mṛgā vīra mām īkśante punaḥ punaḥ
vaktu kāmā iha hi me iṃgitāni anupalakśaye |
verses.translation: "Now all these burly animals are repeatedly looking at me as though to speak to me, oh, brave Lakshmana, this I reckon with their body language as it were.

glosses.meaning: again, again, me, they are seeing
[when their] body language, on gauging by
to me, to say [something,] they desire, now - as it were.

verses.devanagari:
तान् तु दृष्ट्वा नरव्याघ्र राघवः प्रत्युवाच ह
क्व सीत इति निरीक्षन् वै बाष्प संरुद्धया गिरा |
verses.iast:
tān tu dṛṣṭvā naravyāghra rāghavaḥ pratyuvāca ha
kva sīta iti nirīkśan vai bāṣpa saṃruddhayā girā |
verses.translation: But on seeing them pryingly that tigerly-man Raghava has indeed asked them at once with a voice stifled with tears, "where is Seetha?"

verses.devanagari:
एवम् उक्ता नरेन्द्रेण ते मृगाः सहसा उत्थिता
दक्षिण अभिमुखाः सर्वे दर्शयन्तो नभः स्थलम् |
मैथिली ह्रियमाणा सा दिशम् याम् अभ्यपद्यत
तेन मार्गेण गच्छन्तो निरीक्षन्तो नराधिपम् |
verses.iast:
evam uktā narendreṇa te mṛgāḥ sahasā utthitā
dakśiṇa abhimukhāḥ sarve darśayanto nabhaḥ sthalam |
maithilī hriyamāṇā sā diśam yām abhyapadyata
tena mārgeṇa gacchanto nirīkśanto narādhipam |
verses.translation: When that best king has asked, those animals rose to their feet in a trice and facing themselves southward showed skyward with their snouts. And while running in the direction in which Maithili is taken away they are stopping to look back at that lord of people, Rama. Thus they are repeatedly running, stopping and staring at Rama.

glosses.meaning: those, animals, in a trice, rose to their feet
all of them, south, towards, faced - keeping snouts
in which, direction, she chanced to go

verses.devanagari:
येन मार्गम् च भूमिम् च निरीक्षन्ते स्म ते मृगाः
पुनः नदन्तो गच्छन्ति लक्ष्मणेन उपलक्षिताः |
verses.iast:
yena mārgam ca bhūmim ca nirīkśante sma te mṛgāḥ
punaḥ nadanto gacchanti lakśmaṇena upalakśitāḥ |
verses.translation: By which reason those animals are going in a southerly course on a southerly terrain, and stopping to peer at Rama, and again clamorously adopting the very same southerly course, Lakshmana ascertained that reason.

glosses.meaning: again, clamorously, going [adopting the very same southerly course]

verses.devanagari:
तेषाम् वचन सर्वस्वम् लक्षयामास च इन्गितम्
उवाच लक्ष्मणो धीमान् ज्येष्ठम् भ्रातरम् आर्तवत् |
verses.iast:
teṣām vacana sarvasvam lakśayāmāsa ca ingitam
uvāca lakśmaṇo dhīmān jyeṣṭham bhrātaram ārtavat |
verses.translation: On noticing the lingua franca and even the lingua persona of those animals, that imaginative Lakshmana spoke to his elder brother, alike a striver striving hard for some information.

verses.devanagari:
क्व सीत इति त्वया पृष्टा यथा इमे सहसा उथिताः
दर्शयन्ति क्षितिम् चैव दक्षिणाम् च दिशम् मृगाः |
सधु गच्छावहे देव दिशम् एताम् च नैर्ऋतीम्
यदि तस्य आगमः कश्चित् आर्या वा सा अथ लक्ष्यते |
verses.iast:
kva sīta iti tvayā pṛṣṭā yathā ime sahasā uthitāḥ
darśayanti kśitim caiva dakśiṇām ca diśam mṛgāḥ |
sadhu gacchāvahe deva diśam etām ca nair.hṛtīm
yadi tasya āgamaḥ kaścit āryā vā sā atha lakśyate |
verses.translation: "Oh, godly brother, when you have asked these animals, 'where is Seetha,' they quickly rose to their feet, and as to how they are showing the track on the ground and the southern direction as well, thereby we may, for sure, go south-westward to know whether there is some information about her, or else, even that noble lady herself may be available there..."

glosses.meaning: whether, about her, [if available, we get it]
she, noble lady, either, may be seen.

verses.devanagari:
बाढम् इति एव काकुत्स्थः प्रस्थितो दक्षिणाम् दिशम्
लक्ष्मण अनुगत श्रीमान् वीक्ष्यमाणो वसुन्धराम् |
verses.iast:
bāḍham iti eva kākutsthaḥ prasthito dakśiṇām diśam
lakśmaṇa anugata śrīmān vīkśyamāṇo vasundharām |
verses.translation: On saying "Yes!" to Lakshmana that illustrious Rama of Kakutstha sallied forth to southern direction followed by Lakshmana, scrutinising the earth on his walkway.

glosses.meaning: towards southern, direction, he sallied forth.

verses.devanagari:
एवम् संभाषमाणौ तौ अन्योन्यम् भ्रातरौ उभौ
वसुन्धरायाम् पतित पुष्प मार्गम् अपश्यताम् |
verses.iast:
evam sambhāṣamāṇau tau anyonyam bhrātarau ubhau
vasundharāyām patita puṣpa mārgam apaśyatām |
verses.translation: Those two brothers who are proceeding while discussing among themselves have seen the walkway bestrewn with flowers fallen from a person.

glosses.meaning: in this way, one-to-one, while conversing
fallen, flowers, walkway - a walkway bestrewn with flowers

verses.devanagari:
पुष्प वृष्टिम् निपतिताम् दृष्ट्वा रामो मही तले
उवाच लक्ष्मणम् वीरो दुःखितो दुःखितम् वचः |
verses.iast:
puṣpa vṛṣṭim nipatitām dṛṣṭvā rāmo mahī tale
uvāca lakṣmaṇam vīro duḥkhito duḥkhitam vacaḥ |
verses.translation: That valiant Rama who is anguished to see the drizzle of flowers fallen on the surface of earth spoke this word to Lakshmana who is equally anguished.

verses.devanagari:
अभिजानामि पुष्पाणि तानि इमानि इह लक्ष्मण
अपिनद्धानि वैदेह्या मया दत्तानि कानने |
verses.iast:
abhijānāmi puṣpāṇi tāni imāni iha lakṣmaṇa
apinaddhāni vaidehyā mayā dattāni kānane |
verses.translation: "I recognise these flowers that are fallen here, oh, Lakshmana. In forest I gave them to Vaidehi and she tucked these very flowers in her bun.

glosses.meaning: in forest, by me, given - these flowers

verses.devanagari:
मन्ये सूर्यः च वायुः च मेदिनी च यशशिविनि
अभिरक्षन्ति पुष्पाणि प्रकुर्वन्तो मम प्रियम् |
verses.iast:
manye sūryaḥ ca vāyuḥ ca medinī ca yaśaśivini
abhirakśanti puṣpāṇi prakurvanto mama priyam |
verses.translation: "These flowers are carefully safeguarded by the sun, as they are unwithered yet, by air as they are unswept by it, and by the glorious earth, as they are unspoilt by that, thus I deem that these naturals, sun, air, and earth are really proffering a helping hand to me.

glosses.meaning: to me, obliging, by doing - proffering a helping hand

verses.devanagari:
एवम् उक्त्वा महाबाहुः लक्ष्मणम् पुरुषर्षभम्
उवाच रामो धर्मात्मा गिरिम् प्रसवण आकुलम् |
verses.iast:
evam uktvā mahābāhuḥ lakṣmaṇam puruṣarṣabham
uvāca rāmo dharmātmā girim prasavaṇa ākulam |
verses.translation: On saying thus to best one among men Lakshmana, that virtue-souled and dextrous Rama asked the mountain that is uproarious with rapids.

glosses.meaning: one that is with rapids, uproarious

verses.devanagari:
कच्चित् क्षिति भृताम् नाथ दृष्टा सर्वांग सुंदरीम्
रामा रम्ये वनोद् देशे मया विरहिता त्वया |
verses.iast:
kaccit kśiti bhṛtām nātha dṛṣṭā sar.hvāṃga suṃdarīm
rāmā ramye vanod deśe mayā virahitā tvayā |
verses.translation:
"Oh, lord among the earth-bolstered mountains, have you somehow seen a beauty by all her limbs, foregone by me in beautiful woodlands?"

Reply of mountain to Rama:"Oh, lordly bolsterer of earth, lord Rama, I have somehow seen a beauty by all her limbs, foregone by you in beautiful woodlands.'
notes: This question contains a reply to Rama in a sort of jugglery of words / parsing as in - able was I ere I saw Elba. kshiti bhR^itaam naatha 'of earth, among bolsterers, lord; oh, lordly bolsterer of earth, oh, king Rama; tvyaa virahitaa 'by you, foregone...' maya dR^iSTaa iti kaschit, kaschit= kaama pravedane ' by me, seen...'

When the question itself becomes an answer it is citra alankaara and the mountain gave that reply in an echo of Rama's verbiage. Rama takes this as a mere echo of the mountain, but not a clear reply, and thus angering at it he wants to splinter it down, as said in next lines.

glosses.meaning: earth, among bolstered ones, lord [oh, lordly mountain / oh, king]
without [left out, foregone] sarva anga sundariim = all, limbs, beauteous one

verses.devanagari:
क्रुद्धो अब्रवीत् गिरिम् तत्र सिंहः क्षुद्र मृगम् यथा
ताम् हेम वर्णाम् हेम अंगीम् सीताम् दर्शय पर्वत |
यावत् सानूनि सर्वाणि न ते विध्वंसयामि अहम्
verses.iast:
kruddho abravīt girim tatra siṃhaḥ kṣudra mṛgam yathā
tām hema varṇām hema aṃgīm sītām darśaya parvata |
yāvat sānūni sar.hvāṇi na te vidhvaṃsayāmi aham
verses.translation: Because his question is unanswered he is enraged as with a lion enraging at a puny animal, and then he spoke to the mountain, "show me that golden tinged, golden limbed Seetha, oh, mountain, no sooner than I devastate all your apices, apiece..."

glosses.meaning: [like a] lion, with a puny, animal, as with

verses.devanagari:
एवम् उक्तः तु रामेण पर्वतो मैथिलीम् प्रति |
दर्शयन् इव ताम् सीताम् न दर्शयत राघवे
verses.iast:
evam uktaḥ tu rāmeṇa parvato maithilīm prati |
darśayan iva tām sītām na darśayata rāghave
verses.translation: When Rama spoke to the mountain in this way, that mountain echoed as if it is revealing Seetha, but actually it has not revealed Seetha to Raghava.
notes: When the mountain replied echoing the same words of Rama, Rama deemed it silent on other account of Seetha, but just said 'I have seen Seetha...' Hence, that mountain said anything but a proper indication, thus it has dishonoured Rama - Maheshvara Tiirtha. The mountain appeared to have said something but kept mum on other details - Govindaraja. In either way it silent on other details for fear of later time atrocity of Ravana, thereby Rama wanted to subject it to his arrows atrocity, now itself.

glosses.meaning: in that way, which is spoken to
her, revealing, as though - by its echo

verses.devanagari:
ततो दाशरथी राम उवाच शिलोच्चयम् |
मम बाण अग्नि निर्दग्धो भस्मी भूतो भविष्यसि
असेव्यः सततम् चैव निस्तृण द्रुम पल्लवः |
verses.iast:
tato dāśarathī rāma uvāca śiloccayam |
mama bāṇa agni nirdagdho bhasmī bhūto bhaviṣyasi
asevyaḥ satatam caiva nistṛṇa druma pallavaḥ |
verses.translation: Then Rama of Dasharatha said to the hefty mountain, "When the infernos of my arrows will burn you down completely and when you will be pared down ashes, you shall be grassless, treeless and tender-leafless, and thus you become a meritless mountain... hence, show Seetha before becoming so...

glosses.meaning: to mountain, hefty one, said to
to my, arrow's, inferno, completely burnt
not, adorable [unworthy to animals or trees, a meritless mountain]

verses.devanagari:
इमाम् वा सरितम् च अद्य शोषयिष्यामि लक्ष्मण
यदि न आख्याति मे सीताम् अद्य चन्द्र निभ आननाम् |
verses.iast:
imām vā saritam ca adya śoṣayiṣyāmi lakṣmaṇa
yadi na ākhyāti me sītām adya candra nibha ānanām |
verses.translation: "Lakshmana, if this River Godavari is not going to tell me immediately about that moonshine-faced Seetha, now I will dry her up...

glosses.meaning: to me, not, going to tell, if

verses.devanagari:
एवम् प्ररुषितो रामो दिधक्षन् इव चक्षुषा
ददर्श भूमौ निष्क्रांतम् राक्षसस्य पदम् महत् |
त्रस्तया राम काङ्क्षिण्याः प्रधावन्त्या इतः ततः
राक्षसेन अनुवृत्तया वैदेह्या च पादानि तु |
verses.iast:
evam praruṣito rāmo didhakṣan iva cakṣuṣā
dadarśa bhūmau niṣ.hkrāṃtam rākṣasasya padam mahat |
trastayā rāma kāñkśiṇyāḥ pradhāvan.htyā itaḥ tataḥ
rākśasena anuvṛttayā vaidehyā ca pādāni tu |
verses.translation: This way when Rama is highly infuriated and who appeared to burn down anything just with his eyes, then he has seen on the ground gigantic footprints of a demon, and the footprints of Vaidehi, who appeared to have run fearfully here and there in a helter-skelter manner expecting the arrival of Rama, and which footprints are heavily trodden by a demon who followed her.

glosses.meaning: this way, one who is highly, infuriated
with eyes, to burn down, as though
by demon, she who is followed

verses.devanagari:
स समीक्ष्य परिक्रान्तम् सीताया राक्षसस्य च
भंगम् धनुः च तूणी च विकीर्णाम् बहुधा रथम् |
संभ्रांत हृदयो रामः शशंस भ्रातरम् प्रियम्
verses.iast:
sa samīkṣya parikrāntam sītāyā rākṣasasya ca
bhaṃgam dhanuḥ ca tūṇī ca vikīrṇām bahudhā ratham |
sambhrāṃta hṛdayo rāmaḥ śaśaṃsa bhrātaram priyam
verses.translation: On scrutinising the overly trodden footprints of Seetha and the demon, and a broken bow, broken quiver, and broken and variously bestrewn chariot also, then Rama became baffle-hearted and said to his dear brother Lakshmana.

glosses.meaning: overly trodden - ground by way of footprints

verses.devanagari:
पश्य लक्ष्मण वैदेह्याः कीर्णाम् कनक बिन्दवः |
भूषणानाम् हि सौमित्रे माल्यानि विविधानि च
verses.iast:
paśya lakṣmaṇa vaidehyāḥ kīrṇām kanaka bindavaḥ |
bhūṣaṇānām hi saumitre mālyāni vividhāni ca
verses.translation: "See Lakshmana, many beads of jewellery and many bits of garlands of Vaidehi have indeed fallen down, and oh, Soumitri, they are strewn around...

glosses.meaning: oh, son of Sumitra, oh, Lakshmana
many, [bits of] garlands, also - have fallen.

verses.devanagari:
तप्त बिन्दु निकाशैः च चित्रैः क्षतज बिन्दुभिः |
आवृतम् पश्य सौमित्रे सर्वतो धरणी तलम्
verses.iast:
tapta bindu nikāśaiḥ ca citraiḥ kṣataja bindubhiḥ |
āvṛtam paśya saumitre sarvato dharaṇī talam
verses.translation: "Also the surface of the earth is everywhere interspersed with big and small blood drops that are akin to golden droplets, you see them Saumitri...

glosses.meaning: molten [golden,] droplets, equal in shine, also
variedly [big and small,] blood, with drops

verses.devanagari:
मन्ये लक्ष्मण वैदेही राक्षसैः काम रूपिभिः |
भित्त्वा भित्त्वा विभक्ता वा भक्षिता वा भविष्यति
verses.iast:
manye lakṣmaṇa vaidehī rākṣasaiḥ kāma rūpibhiḥ |
bhittvā bhittvā vibhaktā vā bhakṣitā vā bhaviṣyati
verses.translation: "I think Lakshmana, guise changing demons would have ripped and rived Vaidehi, or divided her into pieces, or they might have gluttonised her.

glosses.meaning: she will be [she would have been]

verses.devanagari:
तस्या निमित्तम् वैदेह्या द्वयोः विवदमानयोः |
बभूव युद्धम् सौमित्रे घोरम् राक्षसयोः इह
verses.iast:
tasyā nimittam vaidehyā dvayoḥ vivadamānayoḥ |
babhūva yuddham saumitre ghoram rākṣasayoḥ iha
verses.translation: "A deadly clash has occurred here, Soumitri, while two demons were clashing between themselves on account of Vaidehi...

glosses.meaning: for her, of Vaidehi, on account of
those who are clashing for her

verses.devanagari:
मुक्ता मणि चितम् च इदम् तपनीय विभूषितम् |
धरण्याम् पतितम् सौम्य कस्य भग्नम् महत् धनुः
राक्षसानाम् इदम् वस्त सुराणाम् अधवा अपि |
verses.iast:
muktā maṇi citam ca idam tapanīya vibhūṣitam |
dharaṇyām patitam saumya kasya bhagnam mahat dhanuḥ
rākśasānām idam vasta surāṇām adhavā api |
verses.translation: "Oh, gentle Lakshmana, studded with pearls and gems this great bow of someone is beautifully decorated, but it is fragmented and fallen to earth. Oh, dear boy, Lakshmana, this bow may perhaps belong to demons, or else to gods...

verses.devanagari:
तरुण आदित्य संकाशम् वैदूर्य गुलिका चितम्
विशीर्णम् पतितम् भूमौ कवचम् कस्य कांचनम् |
verses.iast:
taruṇa āditya saṃkāśam vaidūrya gulikā citam
viśīrṇam patitam bhūmau kavacam kasya kāṃcanam |
verses.translation: "Studded with lapis gem beads this golden armour of someone is similar to the rising sun in its shine, but it is splintered and fallen to earth...

verses.devanagari:
छत्रम् शत शलाकम् च दिव्य माल्य उपशोभितम्
भग्न दण्डम् इदम् कस्य भूमौ सौम्य निपातितम् |
verses.iast:
chatram śata śalākam ca divya mālya upaśobhitam
bhagna daṇḍam idam kasya bhūmau saumya nipātitam |
verses.translation: "This hundred-spoked regal-parasol of someone is embellished with divine festoons, but oh, gentle Lakshmana, its central-shaft is wrecked and it is felled to earth...

verses.devanagari:
कान्चन उरः छदाः च इमे पिशाच वदनाः खराः
भीम रूपा महाकायाः कस्य वा निहता रणे |
verses.iast:
kāncana uraḥ chadāḥ ca ime piśāca vadanāḥ kharāḥ
bhīma rūpā mahākāyāḥ kasya vā nihatā raṇe |
verses.translation: "These ghost-faced mules with golden breastplates are macabre in form and massive in frame, but they are hewed down in war, whose are they, either...

glosses.meaning: golden, chest, covered with coverings [breastplates,] also

verses.devanagari:
दीप्त पावक संकाशो द्युतिमान् समर ध्वजः
अपविद्धः च भग्नः च कस्य सांग्रामिको रथः |
verses.iast:
dīpta pāvaka saṅkāśo dyutimān samara dhvajaḥ
apaviddhaḥ ca bhagnaḥ ca kasya sāṅgrāmiko rathaḥ |
verses.translation: "Somebody's combat-chariot is irradiant and similar in shine to the flaring fire with a war-pennon, but it is broken and battered down, as well...

verses.devanagari:
रथ अक्ष मात्रा विशिखाः तपनीय विभूषणाः
कस्य इमे निहता बाणाः प्रकीर्णा घोर दर्शनः |
verses.iast:
ratha akṣa mātrā viśikhāḥ tapanīya vibhūṣaṇāḥ
kasya ime nihatā bāṇāḥ prakīrṇā ghora darśanaḥ |
verses.translation: "These frightful looking arrows of somebody are gilded and they are as much as a chariot's axle in their thickness, but their arrowheads are shred and they are manifoldly shredded and strewn around...
notes: The sizes of Ravana's arrows are calculated differently. This ratha aksha maatra is taken as the length of chariot's wheel and thus it is said four-hundred inches or some 33 feet, which is unacceptable to some as Ravana did not travel in his chariot with a mega body. In another way aksha is taken as the 'eye of axle...' Then the diameter of his arrow is said, 'as thick as an axle...' Some others said the size of arrow is eighty-four inches according to shilpa shaastra 'science of chariot making...' taking this 'eye of axle' into consideration.

glosses.meaning: chariot's, axle / crossbar, as much as
without [shred,] arrowheads / having very sharp arrowheads

verses.devanagari:
शरावरौ शरैः पूर्णौ विध्वस्तौ पश्य लक्ष्मण
प्रतोद अभीशु हस्तो अयम् कस्य वा सारथिः हतः |
verses.iast:
śarāvarau śaraiḥ pūrṇau vidhvastau paśya lakśmaṇa
pratoda abhīśu hasto ayam kasya vā sārathiḥ hataḥ |
verses.translation:
"Lakshmana, you see these two quivers packed with arrows are completely shattered, and the charioteer is drop dead with whip and bridles still in his hands... whose charioteer he might be!

Lakshmana, you see... these two armours, one belonging to the combatant from this chariot [that is ripped off by Jataayu and fallen from the body of Ravana,] and the other belonging to this charioteer, both are encrusted fully with arrows [when Jataayu winnowed the very same arrows shot by Ravana with both of his wings and thus shot them back,] thus the two armours are completely shattered... and the charioteer is drop dead with whip and bridles in his hand... either he... whose is he... and where is the presiding combatant of this chariot....
notes: The word used here for quivers is sharaavara and for this Dr. Satya Vrat says: 'Another word which is also not noticed by Monier Williams is sharaavara. It means an armour kavaca and occurs at least twice in the Ramayana...' Here and at 3-51-14 of this canto and there it was used in the meaning of armour. If this meaning of armour is adopted here also, then the meaning of the above verse may somewhat be,

verses.devanagari:
पदवी पुरुषस्य एषा व्यक्तम् कस्य अपि राक्षसः
वैरम् शत गुणम् पश्य मम तैः जीवित अंतकम् |
verses.iast:
padavī puruṣasya eṣā vyaktam kasya api rākśasaḥ
vairam śata guṇam paśya mama taiḥ jīvita aṃtakam |
verses.translation: "Evidently this is the modus operandi of someone who is a male demon, and you see how my animosity has become hundredfold to eradicate them...
notes: This is the reply to Seetha for she wanted no animosity could be nurtured towards the demons without a cause, in the opening chapters of this Aranya Kanda. When she herself became a cause for that animosity, now Rama is indicating the effect of that cause, in saying: 'I have some animosity towards these demons, but I have not eliminated them sweepingly, but for some demons occasionally... I thought that Seetha strayed her way, or eaten away by some pauperised paltry demon... but on seeing the massive footprints I consider this as a calculated and culpable crime... now that my animosity is multiplied hundredfold, whole of the demonic race will be eliminated...'

verses.devanagari:
सुघोर हृदयैः सौम्य राक्षसैः काम रूपिभिः
हृता मृता वा सीता हि भक्षिता वा तपस्विनी |
न धर्मः त्रायते सीताम् ह्रियमाणाम् महावने
verses.iast:
sughora hṛdayaiḥ saumya rākṣasaiḥ kāma rūpibhiḥ
hṛtā mṛtā vā sītā hi bhakṣitā vā tapasvinī |
na dharmaḥ trāyate sītām hriyamāṇām mahāvane
verses.translation: "The highly stony-hearted demons that are guise-changers by their wish have either abducted, or killed or gluttonised saintly Seetha... but, they say that rectitude saves such saintly persons... yet that rectitude has not saved Seetha while she is being abducted in great forest...
notes: Dharma or Righteousness does not go on safeguarding either its adherents or antagonists, everyone, everywhere, everlastingly. dharmo rakshati rakshitaH and suchlike sayings are also time-bound and when the time is negative aapatsu raksha ko dharmaH 'in difficulties which rightness safeguards?' is the ensuing dilemma.

glosses.meaning: rectitude, not, saves - has not saved her.

verses.devanagari:
भक्षितायाम् हि वैदेह्याम् हृतायाम् अपि लक्ष्मण |
के हि लोके प्रियम् कर्तुम् शक्ताः सौम्य मम ईश्वराः
verses.iast:
bhakṣitāyām hi vaidehyām hṛtāyām api lakṣmaṇa |
ke hi loke priyam kartum śaktāḥ saumya mama īśvarāḥ
verses.translation: "Whether Vaidehi is taken away or taken in by some unknown being, oh, gentle Lakshmana, then who are the gods who can possibly be benignant to me in this world...
notes: 'No god can possibly be non-benignant to me, either in this world or in the other...' Govindaraja.

verses.devanagari:
कर्तारम् अपि लोकानाम् शूरम् करुण वेदिनम् |
अज्ञानात् अवमन्येरन् सर्व भूतानि लक्ष्मण
verses.iast:
kartāram api lokānām śūram karuṇa vedinam |
aGYānāt avamanyeran sarva bhūtāni lakṣmaṇa
verses.translation: "Lakshmana, someone, even if He were a Creator of Worlds, or an Omnipotent, if He were to be lenient at heart or in His actions, He will be disrespected by all beings, owing to the unenlightenment of those beings...

verses.devanagari:
मृदुम् लोक हिते युक्तम् दांतम् करुण वेदिनम् |
निर्वीर्य इति मन्यन्ते नूनम् माम् त्रिदश ईश्वराः
verses.iast:
mṛdum loka hite yuktam dāṃtam karuṇa vedinam |
nir.hvīrya iti manyante nūnam mām tridaśa īśvarāḥ
verses.translation: "I who am mellowly, magnanimous, merciful and yoked only to the wellbeing of all worlds, such as I am, all of the heavenly gods deem me as non-Omnipotent... it is definite...
notes: Annex: 'Even if I am capable of creating, maintaining, and destructing all the worlds, I am lenient, for I am benevolent... but the unwise are unable to know me, the real me... evil-doers are reverenced by one and all, though negatively owing to scare... but a do-gooder is scoffed off, for his deeds are positive and do not yield quick and instant results... and my Omnipotence is looked down as my impotence...' This concept is amplified throughout Bhagavat Gita.

glosses.meaning: world's, wellbeing, one who is yoked to

verses.devanagari:
माम् प्राप्य हि गुणो दोषः संवृत्तः पश्य लक्ष्मण |
अद्य एव सर्व भूतानाम् रक्षसाम् अभवाय च
संहृत्य एव शशि ज्योत्स्नाम् महान् सूर्य इव उदितः |
संहृत्य एव गुणान् सर्वान् मम तेजः प्रकाश्ते
verses.iast:
mām prāpya hi guṇo doṣaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ paśya lakṣmaṇa |
adya eva sarva bhūtānām rakṣasām abhavāya ca
saṃhṛtya eva śaśi jyotsnām mahān sūrya iva uditaḥ |
saṃhṛtya eva guṇān sarvān mama tejaḥ prakāśte
verses.translation: "Have you seen Lakshmana how merits like mercifulness, magnanimity and the like are inverted to become demerits on getting at me, thus I am unmerited in forgoing Seetha. As such, as with the sizzle of sun uprisen quelling all the moonshine, now you may see as to how my irradiance radiates quelling all the merits like softness and fairness for the nonentity of all beings proactive to demons, inclusive of demons.

verses.devanagari:
न एव यक्षा न गंधर्वा न पिशाचा न राक्षसाः |
किन्नरा वा मनुष्या वा सुखम् प्राप्स्यन्ति लक्ष्मण
verses.iast:
na eva yakṣā na gaṃdharvā na piśācā na rākṣasāḥ |
kinnarā vā manuṣyā vā sukham prāpsyanti lakṣmaṇa
verses.translation: "Oh, Lakshmana, will the yaksha-s be comfortable now, no; gandharva-s - no; monsters - no; demons - no; either kinnaraa-s or humans - no, none can be comfortable henceforth...

verses.devanagari:
मम अस्त्र बाण संपूर्णम् आकाशम् पश्य लक्ष्मण |
असंपातम् करिष्यामि हि अद्य त्रैलोक्य चारिणाम्
verses.iast:
mama astra bāṇa sampūrṇam ākāśam paśya lakṣmaṇa |
asampātam kariṣyāmi hi adya trailokya cāriṇām
verses.translation: "Now the welkin will be packed with my arrows and missiles, and I will render it as an impassable sphere for the treaders in the triad of worlds...

glosses.meaning: in three worlds, for treaders among them
not, well, flyable - not moveable - as an impassable sphere

verses.devanagari:
संनिरुद्धग्रहगणमावारितनिशाकरम् |
विप्रनष्टानलमरुद्भास्करद्युतिसंवृतम् || - यद्व -
संनिरुद्ध ग्रह गणम् आवारित निशा करम् |
विप्रनष्ट अनल मरुत् भास्कर द्युति संवृतम्
विनिर्मथितशैलाग्रम्शुष्यमाणजलाअशयम् |
ध्वस्तद्रुमलतागुल्मम्विप्रणाशितसागरम् || - यद्वा -
विनिर्मथित शैल अग्रम् शुष्यमाण जल आशयम् |
ध्वस्त द्रुम लता गुल्मम् विप्रणाशित सागरम्
त्रै लोक्यम् तु करिष्यामि संयुक्तम् काल कर्मणा |
verses.iast:
saṃniruddhagrahagaṇamāvāritaniśākaram |
vipranaṣṭānalamarudbhāskaradyutisaṃvṛtam || - yadva -
saṃniruddha graha gaṇam āvārita niśā karam |
vipranaṣṭa anala marut bhāskara dyuti saṃvṛtam
vinirmathitaśailāgram.hśuṣyamāṇajalāaśayam |
dhvastadrumalatāgulmam.hvipraṇāśitasāgaram || - yadvā -
vinir.hmathita śaila agram śuṣyamāṇa jala āśayam |
dhvasta druma latā gulmam vipraṇāśita sāgaram
trai lokyam tu kariṣyāmi saṃyuktam kāla karmaṇā |
verses.translation: "I will make the triad of worlds quiescent by completely blockading all the planetary bodies. The night-maker moon will be barricaded, aurae of fire, air and sun will be devastated, and then everything will be overcast with darkness. Mountaintops will be completely pulverised, water receptacles will be dried out, and trees, creeping-plants and shrubberies will be destroyed, and oceans depleted, thus I will bring the triad of the worlds to nought, relative to the task of Time in extinguishing an era...

glosses.meaning: with planetary, bodies - resulting into quiescence
being dried up, water, receptacles [rivers, lakes]
Time's, with task [in extinguishing an era,] having [relative to]

verses.devanagari:
न ते कुशलिनीम् सीताम् प्रदास्यन्ति मम ईश्वराः
अस्मिन् मुहूर्ते सौमित्रे मम द्रक्ष्यन्ति विक्रमम् |
verses.iast:
na te kuśalinīm sītām pradāsyanti mama īśvarāḥ
asmin muhūrte saumitre mama drakṣyanti vikramam |
verses.translation: "If the gods are not going to safely restore Seetha to me, oh, Soumitri, they can see what my blitzkrieg is, at this very moment...

glosses.meaning: my, onslaught - blitzkrieg, they, will be seeing.

verses.devanagari:
न आकाशम् उत्पतिष्यन्ति सर्व भूतानि लक्ष्मण
मम चाप गुण उन्मुक्तैः बाण जालैः निरंतरम् |
verses.iast:
na ākāśam ut.hpatiṣyanti sarva bhūtāni lakṣmaṇa
mama cāpa guṇa unmuktaiḥ bāṇa jālaiḥ niraṃtaram |
verses.translation: "All beings cannot fly high in the sky, oh, Lakshmana, as there will be a labyrinth of my arrows released from my bowstring, minus an intercolumniation...

glosses.meaning: up and about - they can fly high.

verses.devanagari:
मर्दितम् मम नाराचैः ध्वस्त भ्रांत मृग द्विजम्
समाकुलम् अमर्यादम् जगत् पश्य अद्य लक्ष्मण |
verses.iast:
marditam mama nārācaiḥ dhvasta bhrāṃta mṛga dvijam
samākulam amaryādam jagat paśya adya lakṣmaṇa |
verses.translation: "Bombarded with my iron-shafts this world will be put to disorderliness, Lakshmana, you may now witness how the animals and birds will be dazed and devastated...

verses.devanagari:
आकर्णपूर्णैरिषुभिर्जीवलोकंदुरावरैः || - यद्वा -
आकर्ण पूर्णैर् इषुभिर् जीव लोकम् दुरावरैः
करिष्ये मैथिली हेतोः अपिशाचम् अराक्षसम् |
verses.iast:
ākarṇapūrṇairiṣubhirjīvalokandurāvaraiḥ || - yadvā -
ākarṇa pūrṇair iṣubhir jīva lokam durāvaraiḥ
kariṣye maithilī hetoḥ apiśācam arākṣasam |
verses.translation: "Because of Maithili I will render this mortal world de-demonical, de-phantasmal by force-stretching my unstoppable arrows up to my ears to release them forcefully...

verses.devanagari:
मम रोष प्रयुक्तानाम् विशिखानाम् बलम् सुराः
द्रक्ष्यन्ति अद्य विमुक्तानाम् अमर्षात् दूर गामिनाम् |
verses.iast:
mama roṣa prayuktānām viśikhānām balam surāḥ
drakṣyanti adya vimuktānām amarṣāt dūra gāminām |
verses.translation: "Let the gods witness now the impact of the blaze-crested, thoroughgoing arrows of mine, projected by my wrath and released by my irascibility...

glosses.meaning: those that released - from my bow

verses.devanagari:
न एव देवा न दैतेया न पिशाचा न राक्षसाः
भविष्यन्ति मम क्रोधात् त्रैलोक्ये विप्रणाशिते |
verses.iast:
na eva devā na daiteyā na piśācā na rākṣasāḥ
bhaviṣyanti mama krodhāt trailokye vipraṇāśite |
verses.translation: "That being so, when the triad of worlds is completely ruined by my anger will there be gods, no; demons - no; phantoms - no, none can survive...

glosses.meaning: when tri-world, while being completely ruined
gods, not, in that way - that being so, will be there

verses.devanagari:
देव दानव यक्षाणाम् लोका ये रक्षसाम् अपि
बहुधानिपतिष्यन्तिबाणोघैश्शकलीकृताः | - यद्वा -
बहुधा नि पतिष्यन्ति बाण ओघैः शकली कृताः |
verses.iast:
deva dānava yakṣāṇām lokā ye rakṣasām api
bahudhānipatiṣyantibāṇoghaiśśakalīkṛtāḥ | - yadvā -
bahudhā ni patiṣyanti bāṇa oghaiḥ śakalī kṛtāḥ |
verses.translation: "Whatever worlds of gods, or monsters, or even those of demons are there, they will be splintered and falling down apiece by the fusillades of my arrows...

verses.devanagari:
निर्मर्यादानिमाँल्लोकान्करिष्याम्यद्यसायकैः || - यद्वा -
निर् मर्यादान् इमान् लोकान् करिष्यामि अद्य सायकैः
हृताम् मृताम् वा सौमित्रे न दास्यन्ति मम ईश्वराः |
verses.iast:
nirmaryādānimā.ṇllokān.hkariṣyāmyadyasāyakaiḥ || - yadvā -
nir maryādān imān lokān kariṣyāmi adya sāyakaiḥ
hṛtām mṛtām vā saumitre na dāsyanti mama īśvarāḥ |
verses.translation: "Whether she is abducted, or even if she is killed, oh, Soumitri, if the gods are not going to give back my Seetha I will now jeopardise these worlds with my arrows...

glosses.meaning: to me, not, if going to give back

verses.devanagari:
तथा रूपम् हि वैदेहीम् न दास्यन्ति यदि प्रियाम्
नाशयामि जगत् सर्वम् त्रैलोक्यम् स चर अचरम् |
यावत् दर्शनम् अस्या वै तापयामि च सायकैः
verses.iast:
tathā rūpam hi vaidehīm na dāsyanti yadi priyām
nāśayāmi jagat sarvam trailokyam sa cara acaram |
yāvat darśanam asyā vai tāpayāmi ca sāyakaiḥ
verses.translation: "If my ladylove is not returned indeed in a fine fettle as she was before my running after Golden Deer, I will be annihilating the triad of world in its entirety, together with its mobile and sessile beings, and I will be sweltering the entire universe with my arrows as long as I am not going to get a glimpse of her." Thus Rama gave a vent to his feelings.

glosses.meaning: that way, in form, indeed [in fine fettle - in 'as is where is' condition]
not, they are going to return, if
of her, a glimpse - I am going to get
universe, by arrows, I will swelter.

verses.devanagari:
इति उक्त्वा क्रोध ताम्र अक्षः स्फुरमाण ओष्ट संपुटः |
वल्कल अजिनम् आबद्ध्य जटा भारम् बन्धयत्
verses.iast:
iti uktvā krodha tāmra akśaḥ sphuramāṇa oṣṭa sampuṭaḥ |
valkala ajinam ābaddhya jaṭā bhāram bandhayat
verses.translation: Rama on saying thus with his eyes reddening in fury, his lappet-fold of lips jerking spasmodically, he girded up his jute-cloths and deerskin and twined up the mass of his matted-hair.

verses.devanagari:
तस्य क्रुद्धस्य रामस्य तथा अभूतस्य धीमतः |
त्रि पुरम् जग्नुषः पूर्वम् रुद्रस्य इव बभौ तनुः
verses.iast:
tasya kruddhasya rāmasya tathā abhūtasya dhīmataḥ |
tri puram jagnuṣaḥ pūrvam rudrasya iva babhau tanuḥ
verses.translation: When the disposition of that venturesome and infuriated Rama has become in that way holocaustic, it is like that of Rudra, the All-Inflamer god, when He became like this in earlier times, intending to inflame the Triple-Cities.

verses.devanagari:
लक्ष्मणात् अथ च आदाय रामो निष्पीड्य कार्मुकम् |
शरम् आदाय संदीप्तम् घोरम् अशी विष उपमम्
संदधे धनुषि श्रीमान् रामः पर पुरंजयः |
युग अन्त अग्निः इव क्रुद्धः इदम् वचनम् अब्रवीत्
verses.iast:
lakśmaṇāt atha ca ādāya rāmo niṣ.hpīḍya kārmukam |
śaram ādāya sandīptam ghoram aśī viṣa upamam
sandadhe dhanuṣi śrīmān rāmaḥ para puraṃjayaḥ |
yuga anta agniḥ iva kruddhaḥ idam vacanam abravīt
verses.translation: On saying so that illustrious Rama, the delighter of world, grabbed his bow from Lakshmana and gripped it tightly, unholstered a deadly and dazzling arrow from his quiver which is like a poisonous serpent, and readying it on the bowstring of his bow, that Rama, the vanquisher of enemies fastnesses, who looked like the Ear-End-Fire, spoke this sentence.

verses.devanagari:
यथा जरा यथा मृत्युः यथा कालो यथा विधिः |
नित्यम् न प्रतिहन्यन्ते सर्व भूतेषु लक्ष्मण |
तथा अहम् क्रोध संयुक्तो न निवार्यो अस्मि असंशयम्
verses.iast:
yathā jarā yathā mṛtyuḥ yathā kālo yathā vidhiḥ |
nityam na pratihanyante sarva bhūteṣu lakṣmaṇa |
tathā aham krodha saṃyukto na nivāryo asmi asaṃśayam
verses.translation: "As to how all the created beings cannot counteract the ageing, dying, fate and the Time at anytime, likewise I too am non-countervailed, when I am coalesced with fury, no doubt about it..."
notes: Time is the all-transcending factor and none can countervail it. anena mR^ityu jara aadayoH ashakya pratiikaaraa iti suucitam | tathaa ca droNa parvaaNi - na hi eSha brahma caryeNa na veda adhyayanena ca | na kriyaabhiH na ca astreNa mR^ityoH kashcin nivartayate | kruura sarva vinaashaaya kaalo asau na ati vartate | mahaa bhaarata - dk

verses.devanagari:
पुरा इव मे चारु दतीम् अनिन्दिताम्
दिशन्ति सीताम् यदि न अद्य मैथिलीम् |
सदेव गन्धर्व मनुष्य पन्नगम्
जगत् स शैलम् परिवर्तयामि अहम्
verses.iast:
purā iva me cāru datīm aninditām
diśanti sītām yadi na adya maithilīm |
sadeva gandharva manuṣya pannagam
jagat sa śailam parivartayāmi aham
verses.translation: "If that princess of Mithila, who has suavely and toothy smiles and who causes irreproachability to my character if only I can have a glimpse of her, is not returned to me in fine fettle as she was when she was with me, then I will countermove whole of this universe together with its gods, immortals, humans, florae and faunas, mountains and waters... and whatnot...

glosses.meaning: suavely, teethed [smiles that sparkle her suavely teeth, occasionally]
[one who will] not, [cause any] reproach - she who will not cause any reproach on my character like the burner of universe, killer of birds and animals etc., - if only I can glimpse her
previously, as [she was in fine fettle]
